newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight rate ends steady in liquid market.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight rate ends steady in liquid market.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate was unchanged at 5.5 percent as market was liquid after heavy lending by big local banks, dealers said on Monday.
They said the liquidity improvement was part of Bank Negara's efforts to ease interest rates by injecting funds into the market.
However, there was no confirmation that the big banks were lending for the central bank, which does not usually comment on its open market operations.
Earlier, other interbank rates were also steady at Friday's levels due to the funds injection.
"Rates are around Friday levels. Big banks are still lending one-month," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
"I think authorities are very insistent to keep rates down," said the dealer.
One-month money was at 7.30/40 percent, three-month money was at 7.40/50 percent and one-week rate was at 6.0 percent, all unchanged from Friday.
Bank Negara has over the past month focused on keeping interest rates under check after an abandoned defense of the ringgit through intervention drained six to eight billion ringgit from the system.
It also imposed restrictions on local banks to limit their swap transactions to $2.0 million per overseas customer.

Dealers said this has brought many overseas investors to the market to unload their holdings of Malaysian bonds. "There are a lot of offers for bonds from overseas, but not enough demand," one bonds dealer said.
Interest rate futures were thinly traded on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange to reflect the uncertainty over the direction of interbank rates, futures dealers said.
At the close, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was down four points to 92.45, or an implied yield of 7.55 percent.
December contract was off three points at 92.61, or 7.39 percent, and March 1998 was down two points to 92.67, or 7.33 percent.
